# Kitchen deformables — measured geometry, prior mechanics

All simulation lengths are metres, masses kg, forces N, Young's moduli Pa. These are **offline reconstructions**, not identified material laws. MuJoCo 3.5.0 runs on CPU at 0.001 s with `implicitfast`. `results.json` records the actual validation run; the JPGs are software MuJoCo renders, not generated illustrations. The original kitchen is not modified.

## Evidence and scale

`evidence/geometry_sources.json` preserves original asset paths, instance transforms and frame IDs. Metric scale is inherited from the supplied depth reconstruction, whose source documentation estimates roughly 4% depth uncertainty. There is no tape measurement. Occlusion, transparent film and reflective steel add uncertainty. “True dimensions” here means metric, depth-supported dimensions rather than arbitrary normalized meshes; it does not mean independently certified dimensions.

Earlier counter_items estimate 80 × 72 × 26 mm rejected in favor of later depth-supported view. |

The towel stripe texture is rectified source photography from f3397. Bag printing is source photography from f2080, with illumination baked in. Sponge and scourer visual surfaces are bound to moving flex control bodies; they are not rigid decoration left behind when the object moves. The collision envelope of the sponge bridges its shallow waist. This small collision/visual discrepancy is explicit, as is the homogenized scourer envelope.

The cloth rest coordinates start in the observed folded configuration. The test checks gravity/contact relaxation of that configuration, not spontaneous folding of an initially flat towel. No vertex is world-pinned. The fixtures are a handle surrogate and rounded divider surrogate; substitute the real kitchen supports when integrating. `evidence/towel_metric_rectangles.json` also preserves the later QA rectangles: left width/height 244.3/361.2 mm at f0772 and 245.7/347.9 mm at f3397. They differ from the older notes above, illustrating the uncertainty in hem selection and depth. The final 348 mm hanging length agrees with the f3397 QA view and lies about 13 mm below the f0772 estimate. A full camera-registered pixel silhouette fit and an oven-door-opening cloth trajectory fit have not been performed. Drape comparisons use the upstream metric rectangle measurements and visual fold profile, not a claimed new pixel reconstruction.

## Material priors and chosen values

The requested source is `[source workspace]`. Its starting-parameter table is the supplied literature prior; it contains no itemized paper citations, and we do not invent those. Nothing in these static views identifies Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, damping, wetness, friction, areal density or film gauge.

| Object | E | nu | Mass model | Friction | Elastic damping (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Sponge | 20,000 | 0.15 | 12 g, effective envelope density 68.9 kg/m³ | 0.80 | 0.0001 |
| Scourer | 50,000 | 0.02 | 25 g, mesh volume density approximately 143 kg/m³ | 0.40 | 0.01 |
| Both cotton cloths | 500,000 | 0.25 | 450 g/m²; mesh-area mass about 76 g towel / 21 g sink cloth | 0.45 / 0.50 | 0.00001 |
| Bag film | 70,000,000 | 0.43 | 925 kg/m³ × 35 µm × triangle area; about 2.5 g, plus 375 g loaf | 0.25 | 0.000001 |

Exact mesh areas, masses and counts are in `parameters.json`. Sponge density is slightly above the dry-PU 25–60 range, near the cellulose 70–300 range, representing a mixed foam/abrasive pad; its composition and wetness are unknown. The prior E ranges are 20–100 kPa sponge, 50–500 kPa effective scourer, 0.5–2 MPa cotton, and 70–300 MPa LDPE. Scourer E is the modulus of a porous wire aggregate, not the approximately 200 GPa modulus of solid steel.

The towel prior combines 2–4 mm terry thickness with bending rigidity 10–50 µN m. A homogeneous shell with 0.5 MPa and 2 mm would be too stiff in bending. We therefore use **0.8 mm structural thickness**, 2 mm contact thickness (`radius=1 mm`), and independent measured-area mass. The isotropic plate estimate `B = E t³ / [12 (1-nu²)]` is 22.8 µN m, inside the table range. This is an effective cloth model, not solid cotton density inferred from the fluffy visible thickness. It cannot independently fit warp/weft stretch, terry pile and bending.

The bag uses physical 35 µm elastic thickness and 1.2 mm collision thickness. The larger collision envelope prevents a coarse shell from being missed by rigid contacts; it is not a claim that the film is 1.2 mm thick. Linear elastic shells approximate wrinkles but do not model irreversible creases, seam rupture, air pressure or crinkling hysteresis. The rigid loaf is an explicit content approximation; crumb compression and slicing are outside scope.

## Discretization and numerical damping

Sponge: nine bonded `dim=3`, `dof="trilinear"` tetrahedral flexcomps, 324 collision vertices total. Shared corner controls have connect constraints; all regions can translate and rotate through their controls. A single trilinear region only supplies 24 generalized DOFs and cannot represent a local fingertip indentation. The center region was narrowed to 24 mm in X, preserving E while admitting the requested indentation. This is resolution calibration against the requested benchmark, not material identification from video. Adjacent sponge regions do not collide with each other; their bonds supply continuity. External geoms must retain compatible contact masks (bit 1 in their affinity, or bit 2 in their type).

Scourer: one 343-vertex tetrahedral trilinear flex. Towel, sink cloth and bag: triangle flexcomps with `elastic2d="both"`, full nodal translation, nonzero radius and automatic self-collision. No plugins or removed `composite` syntax are required.

Elastic damping is stiffness-proportional Rayleigh damping with units of time. It is distinct from the implicit nodal joint damping used for numerical stability. `parameters.json` records the latter separately. High-E, low-mass film is especially stiff numerically at 1 ms. The final nodal damping is 0.05 N s/m for each volume control, 0.8 N s/m for each cotton node and 40 N s/m for each film node. The bag uses the rigid loaf as a freely moving reference frame, so film damping acts relative to the contents rather than the world. The loaf frame has 0.02 generalized joint damping, a numerical stabilization prior. No film vertices are pinned to the loaf; contacts and relative dynamics remain active. This reference-frame damping approximates a tightly wrapped package and should not be used unchanged for an empty loose bag. These assets are intended for slow manipulation; numerical damping is not measured air drag or a measured recovery time. The initial larger Rayleigh coefficients caused unstable explicit elastic modes and were rejected. Stability at 1 ms is tested, not assumed from the integrator's name. No time-substepping is hidden in the tests.

## Contact experiments

The vertical probe is a dynamic, gravity-compensated 50 g body with a 20 × 20 mm square face and one Z slider. External load is ramped over 0.2 s then held for 0.3 s at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 N. The table in `results.json` gives actual contact force, mesh indentation, probe travel, penetration and velocity. Mesh indentation is the change in the initial center top vertices after a separate 2 s gravity settle. It excludes soft-contact penetration. Recovery is observed for 1 s after removal.

Acceptance: sponge 5–15 mm at 5 N; scourer 2–5 mm at 5 N; monotone load response; actual contact force near the requested force; positive tetrahedral volume at rest; finite states with no MuJoCo instability warnings. The sponge test is near the lower end of the requested range, deliberately retaining the 20 kPa prior rather than weakening the material to force a large indentation. Finite-strain foam crushing and scourer plastic compaction are not validated by this reversible elastic model.

Two dynamic box fingers follow mocap target bodies through weld constraints. Unlike direct teleportation of collision geoms, they have solved velocities and transmit friction. The test closes, records bilateral contact, then raises the target 60 mm. For cloth, it pinches a patch of the front tail while the rest remains over the support; whole-sheet COM lift is therefore smaller than fingertip lift. Bag contents and wrapper displacement are reported separately. These are local fixture tests, not a robot reachability or task-success benchmark.

## Integration boundaries

Use `mjcf/<name>.xml` for the full test fixture and `mjcf/includes/<name>.xml` for the object fragment. Fragments contain named defaults/assets/worldbody and any bonds/skins; include them at the `<mujoco>` root. Every symbol starts `ks_<name>`. Scene timestep/integrator are owned by the parent scene. Never load the rigid proxy and deformable for the same physical instance simultaneously. Proxies are free rigid bodies with one convex hull or a compound of convex cloth slabs; they cannot squeeze, wrinkle or catch individual scourer wires.

The body frame is +Z up. Canonical cloth hems start about 20 mm above the fixture floor, so the nominal source bottom-center transform must subtract that offset. Source instance placements are evidence, not a promise that every canonical origin is interchangeable. A unique prefix is required for a second instance. Sponge/scourer collision flexes are transparent in group 3; their bound skins render by default. For collision inspection, show group 3 and set the corresponding flex alpha to 1.

Sources for simulator semantics: [MuJoCo 3.5 flexcomp](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.5.0/XMLreference.html#body-flexcomp) and [elasticity](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.5.0/XMLreference.html#flex-elasticity). Isaac port instructions and version caveats are in `isaac/README.md`. The existing upstream scene replay remains in `../layout/replay/`; this work adds no new capture and makes no real-time reconstruction claim.

## Final acceptance summary

All five asset tests and the combined-fragment compile test passed. The final 5 N mesh indentation is 5.544 mm (sponge) and 2.499 mm (scourer); at 1 N it is 1.131 and 0.500 mm. The sponge's soft-contact penetration reaches approximately 1.05 mm at 5 N and is reported separately, not counted as material compression.

The towel hangs 347.99 mm below the support top after 2 s. The revised divider radius avoids the initial cloth/fixture overlap and yields 163.07 mm hanging length for the sink cloth. The numerical check verifies bounded motion and no warning/reset; it is not a claim of exact static equilibrium or measured damping. Generalized-speed metrics mix translational and rotational joint units and are labeled accordingly in JSON.

The 60 mm finger-lift command raises the sponge COM 57.1 mm and scourer COM 59.7 mm. Supported towel and sink-cloth patch grasps raise total-sheet COM about 12.2 and 16.9 mm. The final bag wrapper rises 33.2 mm and its loaf 41.1 mm, so package slip and deformation remain visible. No vertex is attached directly to a test finger.

The upstream OBJ surface bounds differed from the adopted model.json/depth dimensions. Visual surfaces are explicitly normalized to the accepted metric dimensions before skin binding; this prevents a visually floating probe above an undersized scourer. Long sponge surface triangles are subdivided so the visible foam can follow local indentation. These are visual representation fixes, not changes to the measured press response.
